title: Introduction (SAMPLE CONTENT)

facts.text: A Class A licence covers a combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the towed vehicle is rated at more than 10,000 pounds.
You must pass a knowledge test and a skills test to get a commercial driver licence.
The skills test has three parts: the vehicle inspection, the basic vehicle control skills, and the on-road driving test.

You must take the air brake knowledge test and the air brake part of the vehicle inspection to drive a vehicle with air brakes. If you do not pass them, your licence gets a restriction against air brakes.
You take the skills test in a vehicle of the same type as the licence class you want.

cards.q: What weight ratings define a Class A licence?
cards.a: A GCWR of 26,001 lb or more, with a towed vehicle rated over 10,000 lb.

cards.q: Which two tests must you pass for a CDL?
cards.a: A knowledge test and a skills test.

cards.q: What are the three parts of the CDL skills test?
cards.a: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control skills, and on-road driving.

cards.q: What happens if you do not pass the air brake tests?
cards.a: Your licence gets a restriction that bars you from driving a CMV with air brakes.

exam.q: Which vehicle needs a Class A licence?
choices: A tractor-trailer with a GCWR of 80,000 lb and a 45,000 lb trailer
A straight truck with a GVWR of 30,000 lb and no trailer
A pickup with a 9,000 lb trailer
exam.why: Class A is a combination with a GCWR of 26,001 lb or more and a towed unit over 10,000 lb.

exam.q: How many parts does the CDL skills test have?
exam.why: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving.

exam.q: What does a driver get if the air brake knowledge test is not passed?
choices: An air brake restriction on the licence
exam.why: The licence carries a restriction against driving a CMV with air brakes.
